system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** Based on the supplied extracts, not the underlying SPA or DD documents. Figures below are proposed buyer negotiating positions, not agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for protected claim categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, reserving exceptions below; 20% leaves the Buyer carrying most warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Each claim must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the proposed deductible leaves substantial losses unrecovered. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General warranties: notification within **18 months**; limitations presumptively extend to all Claims. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, with separate periods for other categories and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months; reject universal application** and allow reasonable notification particulars; latent problems may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share general caps and deadlines. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, all issued shares and absence of encumbrances; no general thresholds. | **Require at least a 100% price cap and a longer, separately agreed claim period**, subject to applicable law; ownership and authority are core acquisition risks. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims, with no express fraud exception supplied. | Express protection for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, including appropriate attribution to Seller representatives. | **Carve these out of caps, thresholds, deadlines and remedy/reliance restrictions**, preserving non-excludable rights; the Seller must not obtain contractual protection for its fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identifiable warranties. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, indexed disclosures and a frozen disclosure set**; document availability alone should not shift unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from records. | No knowledge bar; alternatively, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without imputation or duty of enquiry. | **Delete constructive/adviser knowledge and “discoverable” wording**; diligence access should not nullify negotiated warranties or specific indemnities. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite missing final consent and evidence of associated conditions. | A Buyer-benefit completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions on acceptable terms. | **Do not complete without verified effective consent, unless the Buyer expressly waives**; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed and delivery alone may not make consent operative. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment and effective release of relevant security and obligations at Completion. | **Require an agreed payoff/release mechanism and direct payment from Seller proceeds**, reflected once in price mechanics; debt-free/cash-free completion must not leave secured debt behind. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, with funding and payroll mechanics documented. | **Include the verified liability and on-costs in completion adjustments/funds flow, backed by an indemnity where needed**; omission must not transfer Seller transaction costs to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment. | Cleared-payment evidence and legally sufficient confirmation of IP ownership/assignment; protection against resulting title and exploitation risks. | **Require title cure before Completion and broaden the indemnity beyond AUD 180,000 to resulting losses and remediation costs**, outside general limitations; paying the invoice alone may not resolve every IP defect. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, expected immaterial; access, scope and notification requirements remain unknown. | Prompt forensic/legal investigation, containment, evidence preservation, assessment of notification duties and allocation of pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation deliverables, remediation covenants and a tailored indemnity; consider retention pending findings**; uncertainty supports protection, not an assumption of either a confirmed breach or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are ordinary-course operating costs. | Aggregate review of timing, commitments, termination rights, accruals and treatment under price mechanics/interim covenants. | **Assess the AUD 330,000 package together before accepting its classification**; related commitments may require consent or adjustment, but are not automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations and exclusive remedies apply to every Claim unless expressly excepted. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, payment/completion obligations and fraud. | **Insert explicit category exclusions and an overriding precedence clause**; broad “all Claims” wording could otherwise defeat separately negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, ownership, encumbrances, options and other equity rights, plus valid transfer documentation. | **Verify the register against supporting corporate records, relevant searches and completion deliverables**; the register is important evidence, not a substitute for complete title diligence. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are said to be settled under the general regime. | Expressly agreed tax warranties and pre-Completion tax indemnity, with appropriate tax-specific survival; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Keep both open: seek tax survival aligned to assessment periods, commonly seven years with appropriate extensions, and separately negotiate IP protection**; the Seller’s assertion cannot settle unresolved risk allocation. |

**Priority:** resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay title and completion funding before committing to complete; do not accept the disclosure letter as curing those matters.
=== END ADVICE ===
